help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Everything you need to know to use CryptoView
help.card1.title: What does the dashboard show?
help.card1.desc: The dashboard is your main tracking view. It shows in real time the cryptocurrencies you've added to your personal list.
help.card1.totalCoinsDesc: how many cryptos you are monitoring.
help.card1.trendingUpDesc: how many have a positive change in the last 24 hours.
help.card1.trendingDownDesc: how many had a drop in the last 24 hours.
help.card1.avgChangeDesc: the average percentage change of your entire portfolio.
help.card1.info: Each card shows current price, 24h change, market cap and volume.
help.card2.title: What does "Trending up" and "Trending down" mean?
help.card2.desc: These indicators reflect the price change over the last 24 hours, expressed as a percentage.
help.card2.positiveDesc: A positive badge indicates that the price rose compared to yesterday at the same time.
help.card2.negativeDesc: A negative badge indicates a price drop during that period.
help.card2.coinGecko: The shown percentage is the change_percentage_24h provided by the CoinGecko API.
help.card3.title: How does "Update Prices" work?
help.card3.desc: The Update Prices button on the dashboard performs a real-time query to the CoinGecko API for each cryptocurrency in your list.
help.card3.item1: Prices, changes and volumes are updated with the most recent market data.
help.card3.item2: The process may take a few seconds depending on the number of coins in your list.
help.card3.item3: During the update, the button shows "Updating..." and is disabled to prevent duplicate calls.
help.card3.item4: When finished, the timestamp of the last update is shown at the bottom of the dashboard.
help.card4.title: How often are the data updated?
help.card4.desc: The data do not update automatically unless you enable auto-update in Preferences.
help.card4.item1: Manually: by pressing "Update Prices" on the dashboard or "Update All" in My Cryptocurrencies.
help.card4.item2: The CoinGecko API (free plan) allows up to 10–30 calls per minute. Refreshing too frequently may cause temporary errors.
help.card4.item3: For an educational dashboard, it is recommended to update every 5 or 10 minutes.
